ait.heading: Awareness is the beginning, Integration is Key to
paragraphs: Awareness Integration Theory is Dr. Foojan's six-phase approach to understanding how our experiences, perceptions, emotions, and choices shape our lives.

Rather than presenting AIT as a static diagram, this pathway shows its progression: beginning with awareness, moving inward through perception and self-understanding, integrating emotion and values, and ultimately translating insight into accountability.

steps.title: Awareness
steps.text: Recognize what is happening within you and bring experience into conscious view.

steps.title: Perception
steps.text: Examine how experiences, assumptions, and interpretation influence what you see.

steps.title: Self-Concept
steps.text: Explore how you understand yourself and the identity you carry into your life.

steps.title: Emotional Integration
steps.text: Bring greater understanding and integration to emotional experience.

steps.title: Value Alignment
steps.text: Connect your decisions and behavior with the values that matter most to you.

steps.title: Accountability
steps.text: Translate awareness and alignment into intentional, sustained action.

ait.caption: Six connected phases. One continuous movement from awareness to intentional change.

mira.paragraph: Dr. Foojan's Awareness Integration Theory (AIT) is the foundation of the Foojan App, a guided personal-growth experience with Mira™ by AIT, its integrated conversational AI assistant.

products.image_alt: Foojan App welcome screen shown in a smartphone mockup
products.title: A guided journey toward meaningful change.
paragraphs: Inspired by Dr. Foojan's psychological model, the Foojan App helps you explore important life areas, reflect on your thoughts and emotions, recognize patterns, and practice skills for everyday growth. Guided meditations and structured self-reflection are part of one connected experience.

products.image_alt: Mira™ by AIT conversation shown in a smartphone mockup
products.title: Not just a conversation.
paragraphs: Most AI chatbots are designed to respond to questions. Mira™ by AIT is designed to help you explore the questions behind them.

Built into the Foojan App and grounded in Dr. Foojan Zeine's Awareness Integration Theory, Mira™ supports meaningful conversations about the challenges you're facing. It encourages reflection on thoughts, emotions, and recurring patterns. It also helps you identify practical skills to work on in daily life.
products.highlight: Because meaningful personal growth takes more than answers. It begins with awareness, understanding, and action.

mira.note: Mira™ by AIT is a feature within the Foojan App, not a standalone product. It supports personal growth and emotional wellness and is not a replacement for professional psychotherapy, diagnosis, or medical care.

meet.heading: Dr. Foojan Zeine, *Psy.D., LMFT*
meet.subtitle: Psychotherapist · Author · Educator · International Speaker · Originator of Awareness Integration Theory
meet.intro: Recipient of the 2026 American Association for Marriage and Family Therapy’s Clinical Practice Innovation Award, Dr. Foojan Zeine is the originator of Awareness Integration Theory (AIT) and the founder and president of the International Awareness Integration Institute (IAII). A psychotherapist, life and business coach, author, researcher, educator, and international speaker, she brings three decades of clinical experience to advancing mental health, human development, and purposeful living. Her work connects psychotherapy, scientific research, higher education, professional training, organizational leadership, technology, and public education.
meet.body:
Dr. Zeine helps people understand the experiences and beliefs shaping their lives, heal emotional wounds, and develop the awareness and skills to create meaningful, lasting change. A Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist in California since 1996, she maintains a private practice in San Clemente and provides psychotherapy and coaching in English and Farsi, both online and in person. She works with individuals, couples, families, and groups, addressing intimate relationships, trauma, anxiety, depression, addictive behaviors, domestic violence, parenting, self-esteem, immigration, acculturation, and personal development. Her groups and workshops help participants strengthen communication, understand emotional patterns, and build healthier relationships with themselves and others.

Dr. Zeine developed Awareness Integration Theory as a structured, integrative approach to understanding how thoughts, emotions, behaviors, physical experiences, and core beliefs influence one another. Applied in psychotherapy, coaching, education, and leadership, AIT helps people examine the meanings they have assigned to past experiences, recognize patterns operating in the present, and make intentional choices about their future. Her ongoing work includes developing the model, studying its applications, publishing research, and training professionals to incorporate it into their practice.

Through the International Awareness Integration Institute, established in 2017, she leads the development, research, training, and international application of AIT. The institute offers professional education, training, and certification for psychotherapists, coaches, educators, and other helping professionals. She also established the IAII Virtual Clinic, which provides online psychotherapy, coaching, mind-body and wellness services, groups, and psychoeducational programs. These services reflect her commitment to making psychologically informed care and practical tools for wellbeing accessible across communities and cultures.

Her work in digital mental health began well before online therapy became widely used. From 2000 to 2005, she served as Vice President of Program Development at myTHERAPYnet.com, where her responsibilities included supporting clinical and professional standards for a network of nearly 5,000 therapists offering online services. She also developed and conducted international educational programs on online therapy and coaching. This experience informed her doctoral research on the utilization and benefits of online therapy and her co-authorship of Online Therapy: A Therapist’s Guide to Expanding Your Practice, published by W. W. Norton in 2005.

Continuing this commitment to accessible psychological tools, Dr. Zeine is the co-founder and president of Foojan, Inc., where she contributes the clinical perspective and AIT methodology behind the Foojan App. The app offers guided journaling across 30 areas of life, supporting structured self-reflection and personal growth. She also co-developed Mira, an artificial intelligence companion grounded in AIT principles and designed to support emotional awareness, insight, and skill development. Her research and educational work examine how digital platforms and AI can extend access to psychoeducation and reflective practices.

Dr. Zeine serves as a lecturer at California State University, Long Beach, where she designs and teaches undergraduate courses in Mental Health and Community Wellbeing and Drug and Health, along with a Professional Development course for doctoral students. Her teaching integrates AIT, current research, experiential learning, and practical exercises in self-awareness, emotional regulation, communication, and critical thinking. At Université Paris Cité, she teaches Interaction Analysis in Telepsychotherapy within the CYBER Master’s program, an interdisciplinary collaboration involving Université Paris Cité, the University of Barcelona, and Universidade Lusófona. Her contribution focuses on preparing emerging professionals to understand therapeutic interaction within digital environments.

Her academic preparation includes a doctorate in Clinical Psychology from Southern California University for Professional Studies, a master’s degree in Clinical Psychology with an emphasis in Marriage and Family Therapy from La Jolla University, and a bachelor’s degree in Clinical Psychology and Nutrition from Pacific International University. She also earned a Graduate Certificate in Human Behavior from Harvard Extension School. Her additional training spans motivational interviewing, EMDR, biofeedback, clinical hypnosis, domestic violence intervention, Thought Field Therapy, online therapy, life coaching, and Reiki.

An author and co-author of seven books, Dr. Zeine writes for both professional and general audiences. Her books include Life Reset: The Awareness Integration Path to Create the Life You Want; Awareness Integration Therapy: Clear the Past, Create a New Future, and Live a Fulfilled Life Now; Intentional Parenting, co-authored with Nicole Jafari and Eileen Manoukian; and Awakened Leadership: Utilizing Organization Development and Awareness Integration Theory, co-authored with Behnam Bakhshandeh. She also co-authored Online Therapy with Kathleene Derrig-Palumbo and wrote We, a Persian-language psychological novel exploring romantic relationships. Her contributions to edited volumes address life coaching and the application of Awareness Integration Therapy in trauma-informed care.

Dr. Zeine’s research spans psychotherapy, self-identity, relationships, education, mentoring, addiction, digital mental health, and the connections among psychological experience, neurobiology, and genetics. She has authored or co-authored 25 peer-reviewed journal articles, including work examining AIT in relation to anxiety, depression, self-esteem, self-efficacy, couples therapy, student wellbeing, and self-regulation. Her collaborative publications also explore loneliness, reward processes, addiction recovery, and personalized approaches to mental health. She contributes to scholarly publishing through editorial board and peer-review service for scientific journals and organizations.

Her professional leadership includes developing and directing community mental health organizations. From 2000 to 2017, she served as founder, CEO, and president of the Personal Growth Institute, a nonprofit providing multicultural and multilingual psychological services across six Southern California locations. Her responsibilities included program administration, fundraising, grant writing, and clinical supervision of more than 30 licensed therapists, interns, and trainees. She also founded MyNewLife, a licensed outpatient chemical dependency program offering psychotherapy, workshops, advocacy, and recovery resources.

As Clinical Director and Supervisor at PARS Equality Center, Dr. Zeine develops mental health programming, supervises clinicians, and supports individual counseling, group services, and psychoeducational seminars. Earlier in her career, she directed partial hospitalization programs, provided therapy for at-risk adolescents, and developed transitional housing services for women and children affected by domestic violence. These experiences continue to inform her attention to trauma, cultural context, family systems, and access to care.

Dr. Zeine also brings psychological awareness into business and organizational life. Her coaching, teaching, and leadership writing address communication, professional growth, emotional responsibility, and the relationship between personal patterns and organizational functioning. Through Awakened Leadership and her broader professional work, she connects AIT with organization development to help leaders become more intentional in their decisions, relationships, and workplace practices.

An international keynote speaker and workshop facilitator, she has presented at universities and professional conferences around the world, including Harvard, MIT, UCLA, USC, and UCSB. Her speaking topics include AIT, trauma recovery, addiction, couples and family relationships, parenting, cultural adaptation, leadership, and digital innovation in mental health. She has presented for major psychotherapy and addiction organizations, including the American Association for Marriage and Family Therapy, the California Association of Marriage and Family Therapists, and the California Consortium of Addiction Programs and Professionals.

Dr. Zeine extends psychological education to the public as host of InnerVoice—A Heartfelt Chat with Dr. Foojan and through her YouTube channel. Her conversations explore healing, relationships, self-awareness, mind-body wellbeing, leadership, and conscious living. Her media appearances include Dr. Phil, The Jenny McCarthy Show on SiriusXM, Fox television, and numerous radio and podcast programs. Her writing and expert contributions have appeared in outlets including Psychology Today, Huffington Post, Reader’s Digest, Men’s Journal, and YourTango.

Her community and professional service includes roles on the Executive Board of the Iranian American Women’s Foundation, the Scientific Advisory Board of JC’s Recovery & Counseling Center, and the Advisory Board of PARS Equality Center. She also participates in professional communities devoted to psychology, marriage and family therapy, medicine, and continuing education.

Across clinical care, teaching, research, writing, leadership, and technology, Dr. Foojan remains committed to helping people bring awareness into everyday life. Her mission is to make tools for healing and human development increasingly accessible, equipping individuals and communities to clear the past, create a new future, and live a fulfilled life now.
